required_outcomes: Recognises that the troubleshooting checks were sent to the tenant minutes ago (events 005 and 006, the same email twice) and that the next step depends on his answer.
Records that the landlord has already agreed to an engineer attending (event 008), so no further landlord approval is needed if the checks do not fix the door.
Leaves the request on hold with a dated review of two to four days to chase the tenant if he does not reply, and sends no further message to anyone now.
acceptable_alternatives: A one-line note to the tenant apologising for the duplicate email, without repeating the checks.
A dated follow-up instead of a hold.
positive_behaviours: Notices the duplicate send and does not add a third copy.
Does not repeat the warning that the tenant may be liable for a call-out.
red_flags: Assigning an engineer before the tenant has had a chance to try the checks.
prohibited_actions: Asking the landlord to approve the call-out again.
critical_failures: Telling the tenant or the landlord that an engineer is booked or a visit date is set when no provider has been assigned.
